purpose: Measure the complete scalar/direct and batched/graph GPU execution routes at declared sizes with full controller, force and contact evidence. This is execution development, not candidate training or physical qualification.
initialization: Fresh native data and fresh controller/provider memory for every declared trial. Same default S169 pose and one-seed initial native-Y velocity shared across all cells and both routes; no state reset after physics begins. Capture must leave the initial qpos, qvel and clock unchanged.
sampling: Both routes retain every completed internal state, held solver input, named force pair, contact, capacity counter and every portable/provider decision. Graph capture copies five internal snapshots into preallocated device history before the next step1 clears force sensors; host reads occur after graph launch. Prepared observations use checked production-adapter readback and the retained contact compatibility copy. CPU dynamics are forbidden.
coverage: complete host scalar/batch portable and provider path
per-substep force samples before sensor reset
complete contact allocation and compatibility-view joins
graph capture does not advance initial worlds
every trial, cell and timing row retained
bounded owned worker and complete zero-world gate
successor_change: Optional batched host calls, captured GPU split steps and device-buffered complete internal evidence. Consumed scalar campaigns and their declarations stay unchanged.
timing: Three fresh trials per arm and batch size; order alternates by repeat plus size index. Retain all 120 outer commands per trial. First 24 are declared warm-up, last 96 form measured totals. Setup, cold JIT/graph capture, all warm-up timings and full measured section timings remain reported. Combined route comparison only; graph, batching and buffered readback effects are not separately identified. No statistical superiority or trajectory equivalence decision.
